To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the current DNS infrastructure is a single point of failure, and is not designed for the scale of today’s Internet; 2) the DNS is the only Internet infrastructure that is not designed to scale, and it is the only infrastructure where the root name servers have been the bottleneck for years, and 3) the current DNS is a single point for attacks.
the proposed method of anycast-based load balancing is effective, scalable and efficient in the presence of both static and dynamically changing traffic conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a distributed load-balancing and mapping system based on the anycast addressing scheme.
the development of a new approach to the design of a distributed load balancing system.
the problem of providing scalable and efficient content distribution over the Internet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the invention relates to a distributed load balancing system and method for extending the use of anycast addresses.
the present invention provides a distributed load balancing system and method that extends anycast to a plurality of servers in a network.

the present invention provides a system, method, and apparatus for providing distributed load-balancing based on anycast to a plurality of servers within a network, comprising a DNS server configured to respond to domain name requests received from one or more clients; the DNS server maintaining an anycast IP address set associated with a domain name, and the DNS server responding to a client request by selecting one or more anycast IP addresses in the anycast IP address.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed and implemented a new system for the distribution of load in the DNS, based on anycast, that can be used to improve the performance and availability of DNS servers.
we have proposed a novel approach to provide scalable load balancing and content distribution in a distributed network.
the invention provides a system for load balancing a plurality of servers in a distributed system using an anycast-based approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of anycast is not only a viable option, but also a good one.
the anycast-based CDN architecture is a promising alternative to the client-based CDN architecture, and that it is capable of providing a similar level of performance.

the anycast routing system can be improved by using the DNS to provide a more flexible mechanism for mapping anycast addresses to servers, and by allowing the anycast addresses themselves to be used for server load balancing.
